summary: Revision round 1 (v0.2) of the arc-011 threat model, answering Codex (return for revision) and GLM (fit with fixes): 36 findings checked, 31 valid, 5 partly, 0 not valid (disposition-r1.md). Four fidelity changes withdrawn or made explicit: no interrupt allow-list at circuit set-up (R-52.a, R-63.a); revocation never makes mail DEAD (R-44, R-60); PR-15 limited to resume, takeover unchanged (R-67, R-68); retention per R-35.o; PR-5 binding as R-60.a (2e); no 'allowed peer' class. Over-claims fixed: circuit lifetime from establishment and never reset; revocation split into 7 scopes with reachable and partitioned bounds; SI-9, 13, 17, 19, 21, 22 restated; contiguous receipts; identity-keyed namespaces. Added: ADV-14 and the operator approval device; TH-58..65 (65 threats); SI-29..31 (31 invariants); RR-15..19 (19 residuals); CR-14, CR-15 (15 change requests); OQ-10..14; PR-26..33; invariant-to-CR table (18.2); numbers labelled hypotheses. Drawings D-1 and D-2 corrected and all four re-rendered. Step-1 requirements not changed.

change_requests.what: CR-1 R-45.a, R-26.o and R-44.a conflict with R-7.e (1): with the hub unreachable on a circuit, stages, replies and sender-visible states cannot be hub-first. Local hash-chained log first, replayed on return; reply carried on the circuit; state computed from circuit receipts and labelled unreconciled, UNKNOWN only when nothing can be read; write-ahead intent before hand-over.
CR-2 No requirement says messages are signed by a per-agent key and verified (GP-1; R-34.e (2) says authentication is not required, R-63 relies on a verified key).
CR-3 R-51.a: identity should be (sender identity, conversation id, message id) bound to a content digest, with a CONFLICT outcome for the same id with different content.
CR-4 R-59.a: receipts signed, forward-only, contiguous and bounded by what was stored; random first number; counter rebuilt from the hub record; equivocation outcome; namespace survives key rotation.
CR-5 R-23.a and R-23.e: make 'no peer content in the typed line' firm, constrain ids to 32 hex characters, require a foreground-process check before typing and a re-check just before.

CR-6 R-50 and R-47: frame produced by the receiving adapter with a random boundary, a size cap, two trust classes plus an allow-list fact line (no third class), no peer message as approval, applied to every rail that puts peer text in an agent's context.

CR-7 R-46: add the sender-constrained, connection-bound, scoped credential, establishment nonce and set-up window, lifetime from establishment never reset, signed revocation list with rollback protection and a stale rule, and a stated lifetime. No allow-list check at set-up (R-52.a, R-63.a).

CR-8 R-60 and R-61: fleet admission roster, signed cards, home-hub binding as R-60.a (2e) rules it, project root key, signed hub-key rotation and moved-to statements, no-guess rule at first sight, hub signing key apart from the TLS certificate.
CR-9 R-35, R-45, R-15: say whether the hub copy of a circuit turn carries content, and whether content is protected from token holders and from the hub operator.
CR-10 R-63.a: the default allow-list 'own project plus the operator' has no authenticated operator identity until GP-11 is ruled.
CR-11 R-53.a and R-63: peers should see only reachable yes or no and the version class, not the four reachability fields.
CR-12 R-65.a and R-60: DEAD must be signed, and a resume (not a takeover) needs a host-local check that no process holds the session. R-67 and R-68 unchanged; the earlier takeover check is withdrawn.
CR-13 R-67.a and R-64: role eligibility from operator-signed configuration; grants, allow-lists and roster take effect only with an operator signature or a hub-held verified record. Depends on CR-14.
CR-14 New, touches GP-11 and R-63.a: an operator approval key and device with second factor, single-use short-lived digest-bound approvals, second-channel notice with a delay, offline recovery key.
CR-15 New, touches R-62.a: conversation membership (R-1.e (2) many-to-many, R-62 hand-over) changes only by a signed, countersigned, recorded event or a hand-over under a stated rule.
